title: Christmas Wishes: 40 Card Messages for Everyone You Love
seoTitle: Christmas Wishes: 40 Card Messages for Everyone You Love
description: Christmas wishes for your partner, parents, colleagues and friends. 40 short card messages you can copy, plus tips to write your own in under a minute.
keyword: christmas wishes, christmas card messages, merry christmas
author: BikaFlora
imageAlt: 12 red soap roses with a card for Christmas wishes
html:
Stuck on what to write in a Christmas card? You're not alone. Most of us stare at the blank card longer than we spent choosing the gift. The good news is that a short, warm message works better than a clever one. Below you'll find 40 Christmas wishes sorted by who they're for, from your partner to your boss. Copy one as it is, or change a few words so it sounds like you.

What's a simple Christmas wish? "Merry Christmas! Wishing you a warm, happy season with the people you love."

What should I write in a Christmas card for a colleague? Keep it light and kind, like "Thanks for a great year together. Enjoy the break!"

How long should a Christmas card message be? One to three sentences is plenty. Warmth matters more than length.

Key takeaways

  • A short, specific message beats a long, general one.
  • Mention one real thing you're grateful for, and the card instantly feels personal.
  • Match the tone to the person: playful for friends, warm for family, polite for work.
  • Pair the card with one of our best sellers, so the message stays on their shelf too.

Why does a Christmas card message matter so much?

Many people skip the message because they worry it'll sound awkward. Research says that worry is mostly in our heads. In a study published in Psychological Science, Amit Kumar and Nicholas Epley asked people to write thank-you letters and guess how the receiver would feel (Kumar and Epley, 2018). The writers expected their notes to land as a bit awkward. In fact, the people who read them felt much happier and less awkward than the writers had predicted.

So don't overthink it. A few honest words carry more weight than you expect.

40 Christmas wishes, sorted by who they're for

1. For your partner

  • "Merry Christmas, love. You're my favourite part of every year."
  • "Of all the gifts under the tree, you're still the best one."
  • "Here's to more Christmases, more laughs and more of us."
  • "Thank you for making this year softer, sweeter and so much more fun."

7. For your boss or manager

  • "Season's greetings, and thank you for your support and trust."

8. For clients and business partners

  • "Thank you for working with us this year. Season's greetings from all of us."

10. Short wishes for WhatsApp and Instagram

  • "Peace, love and plenty of food. Merry Christmas!"
  • "Wishing you joy today and all year long."
  • "Merry Christmas and a happy new year from our home to yours."

How do you write your own Christmas wish?

Use this simple three-part pattern:

  1. Greet them. "Merry Christmas, Aunty Rose."
  2. Say one real thing. "Thank you for teaching me how to make your famous curry puffs."
  3. Wish them well. "Wishing you a happy, healthy year ahead."

That's it. Three short lines feel personal because the middle line could only be about them.

Which wishes suit a flower card?

Flower cards are small, so the shorter wishes in each group work best. For a romantic gift, the partner messages pair well with red roses. For mum or grandma, a thank-you style message suits softer colours like pink and lavender, the kind you'll find among our flowers for her.

When you order a bouquet from us, tell us your message on WhatsApp and we'll handwrite it on the card. Prefer to stay a secret? Ask for a blank card instead.

The bottom line

The best Christmas wishes are short, warm and a little bit specific. Pick a message from the list above, add one real detail, and you're done. Whether the card travels with a bouquet across the city or sits on a colleague's desk, it'll mean more to them than you think.

FAQs

Keep it friendly and general. "Wishing you a warm and happy Christmas season" works for neighbours, new colleagues and clients.

What's a good Christmas wish for a non-Christian friend?

"Season's greetings" or "Happy holidays" are kind, inclusive options. Many Malaysians of all faiths also enjoy a simple "Merry Christmas!"

Should I sign my full name on a work Christmas card?

Yes, for work cards. Your full name, or your name and team, helps busy people know who the card came from.

Can a Christmas card message be funny?

Of course, especially for friends and siblings. Just keep jokes kind, and save them for people who know your sense of humour.

title: Meaning of the Number of Roses: What 1 to 99 Roses Say
seoTitle: Meaning of the Number of Roses: 1, 12, 52 and 99 Explained
description: The meaning of the number of roses explained: what 1, 3, 6, 12, 18, 25, 52 and 99 roses say, and how to pick a bouquet for love or a proposal.
keyword: meaning of number of roses, 99 roses, dozen roses
author: BikaFlora
imageAlt: Six red soap roses showing the meaning of number of roses
html:
The meaning of the number of roses is a quiet language: the count says something before the card is even read. One rose says "you're the one", 12 roses mean a whole year of love, and 99 roses say "forever". These meanings come from florist tradition rather than strict rules, but many people know them. This guide explains what each popular number means and which of our handmade soap rose bouquets matches it.

What does 1 rose mean? Love at first sight, or "you're the only one".

What do 12 roses mean? One rose for every month, so a full year of love.

What do 99 roses mean? "I'll love you forever." It's a classic proposal number.

Do the meanings change with colour? Yes. The number sets the message, and the colour adds the feeling.

Key takeaways

  • Small numbers (1 to 6) feel sweet and personal, perfect for early dating or a simple surprise.
  • 12 roses are the classic romantic choice for anniversaries and Valentine's Day.
  • Big numbers like 52 and 99 are made for proposals and milestone moments.
  • Colour changes the message, so choose both together.

Where do rose number meanings come from?

Giving flowers with hidden messages goes back a long way. The Old Farmer's Almanac notes that learning flower symbolism became a popular pastime in the 1800s, when many Victorian homes kept guidebooks to the "language of flowers" (The Old Farmer's Almanac). It also points out that the meanings shifted depending on which guide you read.

Rose numbers work the same way today. Florists around the world share a common set of meanings, but there's room to make a number your own.

The meaning of the number of roses, from 1 to 99

1. One rose: "You're the one"

A single rose is simple and bold. It suits a first date, a small "thinking of you" moment, or someone who prefers a quiet gesture. Since one soap rose on its own can look a little lonely, a small gift box with three roses gives the same sweet message with more presence.

2. Three roses: "I love you"

Three roses stand for three words. The Red Rose Gift Box with Light (RM65) holds exactly three red soap roses in a clear box with warm LED lights, which makes it a lovely bedside gift.

3. Six roses: "I want to be yours"

Six roses often signal a crush that's turning into something more. Heart's Desire (RM93) has six red soap roses with pink baby's breath, wrapped in cream paper with a burgundy bow. It's a gentle way to say how you feel without going too big.

4. Ten roses: "You're perfect"

Ten roses tell someone they're perfect just as they are. Several of our bouquets use ten roses: Pinky Promise in blush pink, Dark Obsession in black for him, and the Ferrero Rocher Red Roses with seven chocolates.

5. Twelve roses: "Be mine for a whole year"

A dozen roses is the most famous number of all. Each rose stands for one month, so together they mean a full year of love. 365 Days of Love (RM102) was built around this idea, with 12 red soap roses in white paper and black mesh.

6. Eighteen roses: a coming-of-age moment

Eighteen roses are a favourite for an 18th birthday, a milestone in many families. They also work as a romantic gift when you want something fuller than a dozen. Midnight Romance (RM93) has 18 white soap roses in black wrapping, a striking look for a birthday that matters.

7. Twenty-five roses: "Congratulations"

Twenty-five roses often mark a celebration, from a promotion to a 25th anniversary. Our two best sellers, the Red Soap Rose Heart Large and the Pink Soap Rose Heart Large (RM140 each), both use 25 soap roses layered into a heart.

8. Fifty-two roses: one for every week

Fifty-two roses mean you've loved someone every single week of the year. It's a grand number for a big anniversary or a surprise that needs to make an entrance. The 52 Roses Heart (RM375) is made to order in the colours you choose.

9. Ninety-nine roses: "Forever"

Ninety-nine roses say "I'll love you for as long as I live". That's why they're a classic choice for marriage proposals. The 99 Roses Heart (RM544) is our grandest design, made to your colour plan with at least 24 to 48 hours' notice.

10. Any number that means something to you

Rules are only half the fun. Some people send roses to match a partner's age, the date they met, or the number of years they've been married. Tell us the number you have in mind, and we'll let you know if we can make it as a custom pre-order.

Does rose colour change the meaning?

Yes. The number sets the message, and the colour adds the feeling. Red roses mean romantic love, pink roses suggest sweetness and thanks, and white roses feel pure and calm. Blue roses, which only exist as soap or dyed flowers, feel rare and special.

How far ahead should you order large rose numbers?

Bouquets up to 25 roses are usually ready-made, so we can deliver them on the same day across KL and Selangor. The 52 and 99 roses hearts are made by hand to your design, so they need at least 24 to 48 hours. If you're planning a proposal, message us earlier so we can agree on colours, timing and the exact place for delivery. Our pre-order collection lists every made-to-order design.

The bottom line

The meaning of the number of roses gives you an easy way to say more with a bouquet. Go small and sweet with one to six roses, classic with twelve, or unforgettable with 52 or 99. Then pick a colour that fits the feeling. Because our roses are made of soap, the message stays on their shelf for months.

A dozen, or 12 roses, means a full year of love, one rose for every month. It's the most popular romantic number.

One to three roses is plenty. It feels thoughtful without putting too much pressure on a new relationship.

Ninety-nine roses stand for everlasting love. Many people choose them because the number says "forever" without words.

Some cultures prefer odd numbers for happy occasions, while others don't mind. If you're unsure, ask the receiver's family or choose an odd number like 3, 25 or 99.

title: What Are Soap Flowers? How They're Made and Why They Last
seoTitle: What Are Soap Flowers? How They're Made and Why They Last
description: What are soap flowers? Learn what they're made of, how long they last in Malaysia's heat, whether they smell, and why they make a long-lasting gift.
keyword: what are soap flowers, soap flower bouquet, soap roses
author: BikaFlora
imageAlt: Pink soap rose heart explaining what are soap flowers
html:
Soap flowers are flowers made from thin sheets of soap, shaped petal by petal to look like real roses, daisies and carnations. They need no water, they don't wilt, and they keep their colour for months. That's why a soap flower bouquet has become one of the most popular gifts in Malaysia. Here's what they're made of, how long they really last, and what to know before you buy your first bouquet.

What are soap flowers made of? Thin, scented soap sheets, cut and shaped into petals.

How long do soap flowers last? Months, as long as you keep them dry and out of direct sun.

Do soap flowers smell? Yes, a light, clean soap scent rather than a strong perfume.

Can you use soap flowers as soap? You can. A petal lathers a little in water.

Key takeaways

  • Soap flowers are real soap, shaped into lifelike petals.
  • They don't need water and won't wilt in hot weather.
  • Humidity and steam are their only real enemies.
  • Each bouquet is handmade, so small differences make every one unique.

What are soap flowers made of, and how does soap become a petal?

Soap itself is centuries old. Encyclopaedia Britannica explains that soap has always been made by heating fats with water and a basic substance, a reaction known as saponification (Britannica). The result is the solid soap you know from your bathroom.

For soap flowers, that soap is pressed into very thin, flexible sheets in many colours. Each sheet is cut into petal shapes, then the petals are layered by hand around a centre to form a bloom. Finally, the bloom is fixed to a stem and arranged with fillers such as baby's breath or caspia.

10 things to know before you buy soap flowers

1. They're real soap, not plastic

Soap flowers are made from soap, not plastic or fabric. Touch a petal and it feels soft and slightly smooth, a bit like a thin bar of soap. Because of this, they look much more natural than silk or plastic flowers.

2. They never need water

There's no stem in water and no vase to refill. That makes soap flowers easy for students in hostels, busy office workers and anyone who travels often. You simply set the bouquet down and enjoy it.

3. They last for months, not days

Fresh flowers in our warm weather usually look their best for only a few days. A soap flower bouquet keeps its shape and colour for months with simple care.

4. They have a light, clean scent

Soap flowers smell gently of soap, not of real roses. The scent is soft enough for a bedroom or office, and it fades slowly over time.

5. They carry no pollen

Since there's no real plant inside, soap flowers release no pollen. That makes them a kinder choice for people with hay fever. If you're sending flowers to a hospital, check the ward's rules first, as some limit any kind of flowers.

6. They can lather if you want them to

Yes, a soap petal really does lather in water. Most people keep their bouquet as decoration, though, because it looks too pretty to use. If you do want to try one, take a petal from the back so the front still looks full.

7. Humidity and steam are their only real weakness

Water and steam soften soap. Keep your bouquet out of the bathroom and away from a steaming kettle or rice cooker, and it'll stay neat. A clear gift box helps too, which is why our flower gift boxes are popular for desks and bedside tables.

8. They come in colours real flowers can't

Soap sheets can be any colour, so you'll find soap roses in sky blue, black and deep navy alongside classic red and pink. Blue Noir For Him, for example, mixes blue and black roses, a look you'd never find in a garden.

9. Every bouquet is handmade, so each is a little different

Because the petals are shaped by hand, no two bouquets are exactly alike. Colours and wrapping can vary slightly from the photo. That's why we send you a photo of your actual bouquet before it leaves us.

10. They cost less per day than fresh flowers

A soap bouquet and a fresh bouquet can cost about the same on the day. The difference is how long you enjoy it. Spread over several months, a soap bouquet works out far cheaper per day. Our bouquets below RM100 start from RM65.

Are soap flowers the same as preserved flowers?

No. Preserved flowers are real flowers treated so they stop ageing. Soap flowers are made entirely from soap and only look like real flowers. Both last a long time, but soap flowers are usually lighter, more colourful and more affordable.

What does a soap flower bouquet look like up close?

Take the Pink Soap Rose Heart Large (RM140) as an example. It has 25 pink and ivory soap roses packed tightly into a heart shape, and it's one of our best sellers. Up close, you can see each petal curling slightly at the edge, just like a real rose.

If you'd like something that lasts even longer than soap, our crochet bouquets are made from yarn and can last for years.

The bottom line

So, what are soap flowers? They're handmade blooms shaped from real soap, designed to look like fresh flowers without wilting. They suit Malaysia's heat, carry a gentle scent and last for months. For a gift that becomes a keepsake rather than a short memory, they're hard to beat.

FAQs

Are soap flowers real flowers?

No. They're made from soap shaped to look like flowers. No real petals or plants are used.

How long do soap flowers last in Malaysia?

They last for months when kept indoors, dry and away from direct sunlight. Steamy rooms shorten their life.

Do soap flowers melt in hot weather?

No, they don't melt in normal room heat. Very high heat, such as inside a parked car, can soften them, so avoid leaving them there.

Are soap flowers safe for children?

title: How to Care for Soap Flowers So They Last for Months
seoTitle: How to Care for Soap Flowers So They Last for Months
description: How to care for soap flowers in Malaysia's humid weather: 10 simple tips on where to keep them, how to clean them and what to do if they get wet.
keyword: how to care for soap flowers, soap flowers, humidity
author: BikaFlora
imageAlt: Pink soap roses in a clear box, showing how to care for soap flowers
html:
Learning how to care for soap flowers takes two minutes, because they have only one enemy: moisture. Keep your bouquet dry, out of direct sun and away from steam, and it'll keep its shape and colour for months. That's really all there is to it. Below are 10 practical care tips for Malaysian homes, plus what to do if your bouquet gets wet or dusty.

Do soap flowers need water? No. Never water them, as water dissolves soap.

Where should I keep soap flowers? Indoors, in a dry room, away from sunlight and steam.

How do I clean soap flowers? Brush the dust off gently with a soft, dry brush.

Key takeaways

  • Moisture is the main thing that damages soap flowers.
  • Bathrooms, kitchens and windowsills are the worst places to keep them.
  • A soft brush or a cool hair dryer clears dust safely.
  • A clear gift box or carry bag protects the petals from dust and knocks.

Why does humidity matter for soap flowers in Malaysia?

Our weather is the reason. Encyclopaedia Britannica describes Malaysia as having high temperatures and high humidity, with heavy rainfall shaped by the monsoons (Britannica). Soap softens when it absorbs moisture, so damp air and steam can slowly change the shape of the petals. The good news is that small habits make a big difference.

How to care for soap flowers: 10 tips to keep them looking new

1. Keep them out of the bathroom

The bathroom looks like a natural home for soap, but it's the worst spot. Steam from showers softens the petals and can make them stick together. Choose a bedroom, living room or office instead.

2. Keep them away from kitchen steam

Rice cookers, kettles and boiling pots all release steam. A bouquet on the kitchen counter takes in moisture every time you cook. Move it to a room further from the stove.

3. Keep them out of direct sunlight

Strong sunlight fades colours over time, especially deep reds and the dark blues in our flowers for him. A shelf away from the window keeps the colours bright. Indirect light is fine.

4. Never leave them in a parked car

A car parked in the afternoon sun gets very hot inside. That heat can soften soap petals and bend the shape of the bouquet. Take it straight inside after you pick it up.

5. Never spray them with water

Fresh flowers love a mist of water, but soap flowers don't. Water dissolves soap, which leaves marks and soft spots on the petals. Skip the spray bottle completely.

6. Don't spray perfume on them

Some people add perfume to refresh the scent. Perfume contains alcohol and water, which can stain or soften the petals. Enjoy the light soap scent as it is.

7. Dust them gently every few weeks

Dust settles on any decoration. Use a soft, dry makeup brush or paintbrush and sweep lightly across the petals. For hard-to-reach spots, a hair dryer on the cool setting, held at a distance, blows dust away without touching anything.

8. Use a box or cover for extra protection

A clear case keeps dust off and lowers the moisture that reaches the petals. That's one reason our boxed designs stay looking new for so long. A glass cloche or display box works well for bouquets too.

9. Hold the wrapping, not the petals

Petals are thin and can bend if you squeeze them. When you move the bouquet, hold it by the wrapping or the base. For travel, our Bouquet Protection Bag (RM6) is a thick, clear carry bag with handles that stops the bouquet from getting crushed.

10. Keep the room cool and dry where you can

Air-conditioned rooms tend to be drier than open-air spaces, which suits soap flowers well. If your home gets very humid during the rainy months, a room with a fan or air-conditioning is the best place for your bouquet.

What should you do if your soap flowers get wet?

Don't panic, and don't rub them. Gently shake off any drops, then leave the bouquet in a dry, airy room to dry naturally. Rubbing a wet petal can smear the soap and leave marks. Once dry, a slightly marked petal can often be turned to face the back of the bouquet.

How long do soap flowers last with good care?

With these habits, a soap bouquet lasts for months. If you'd like something that lasts even longer with almost no care, crochet bouquets are made from yarn and can last for years.

What if your bouquet arrives damaged?

We check every bouquet and send you a photo before delivery. If something still arrives damaged, message us on WhatsApp within 24 hours with photos. After checking, we'll offer a replacement or a refund under our refund policy.

The bottom line

Caring for soap flowers comes down to one rule: keep them dry. Choose a cool room away from steam and sunlight, dust them now and then, and handle them by the wrapping. Do that, and your bouquet keeps looking like the day it arrived for months to come.

FAQs

Can I put soap flowers in a vase with water?

No. Water dissolves soap. Use an empty vase or stand the bouquet on its own.

Why are my soap flowers sticky?

Stickiness usually means they've absorbed moisture. Move them to a drier, cooler room and let them air out.

Do soap flowers fade over time?

Colours can fade slowly in direct sunlight. Keep them out of strong light to stop this.

Can I store soap flowers in a cupboard?

Yes, if the cupboard is dry. Add a sachet of silica gel to soak up extra moisture.

Can I use the petals as real soap?

Yes. Take a petal from the back of the bouquet and use it with water. It lathers a little.
